_about: THE ROUND MODEL (decision round-model; builder G3, 2026-10-12; scripts/sim/rounds.gd reads this). ALEX (decision round-model, 2026-10-11): 'a round per weapon with class, calibre, explosive, path, tracer and blast; a round x material table for impacts; armour and penetration later'. On the proposed properties: '2 rounds - for now' (the proposal is docs/proposals/damage-rounds-cover.md section 2). On the direction: '6 good but we need more here. Let's discuss.' WHAT A WEAPON FIRES decides its look (decision weapon-kinds, Alex: 'Flak would be shells shot that then explode. Machine guns would be bullets which don't.'): every weapon in data/units/*.json names its round (weapons[].round); the cruiser's Main Guns and the bomb drop are specials, named in `specials` below. A ROUND carries: class (what it is), calibre (small, medium, large: it sets the muzzle smoke's and the impact's size, data/fx/fx.json gunfire), explosive (an explosion on landing, or a strike of sparks and dust), path (a straight line, an arc, or a burst in the air), tracer (it draws a tracer: decision tracers-mg), and for an explosive round that has one a pointer to the BLAST TABLE it already has (not moved, not copied: {file, path} resolves to a list of [distance_m, pips]). WHAT A ROUND DOES WHERE IT LANDS is a table of round x MATERIAL (the thing hit; `vocabulary.materials`; each unit file and each line-of-fire cell names one): data/fx/fx.json gunfire. Later, not now (Alex: 'armour and penetration later'): whether a bullet can hurt a tank, and damage per round. THE SEVEN ROUNDS BELOW ARE PROPOSED by builder G3 from the board's table (variants/gunfire/families.json rounds: bullet, small, medium, large) and the proposal's five classes; the class decides the look, the calibre the size: two cannon rounds, two flak shells, and one each of the others. Record shape as the other sim data: {value, _proposed, _reason} or {value, decision, _reason}.

classes._reason: the proposal's five classes (docs/proposals/damage-rounds-cover.md section 2: bullet for machine guns, cannon round for the tank and the nose cannon, flak shell that bursts in the air, shell for the Main Guns, bomb). PROPOSED

calibres._reason: Alex's round-model direction names calibre; the three sizes are the proposal's (small, medium, large) and the gunfire board's size tables (variants/gunfire/families.json classes). PROPOSED

paths._reason: the proposal's three paths: straight (bullets, cannon), arc (shells, bombs), air burst at a height (flak). PROPOSED

materials._reason: THE ONE VOCABULARY for what a round hits (decisions damage-looks, 'the model makes sense', everything names a material, and gunfire-looks, G3: 'the materials told apart by lightness'). The board's table (variants/gunfire/board.json material_table, PROPOSED) said ground; the line-of-fire grid said ground, timber and earthworks; they are now ONE set: metal (planes, armour, ships, the tower's lattice), stone (the bridge, walls, the complex), wood (houses, trees, the barge), earth (open ground, roads, fields, sandbags and earthworks, the AA battery) and water (every depth). The NAMES 'earth' and 'wood' are the lead's (2026-10-12, PROPOSED): the board's ground and the grid's timber renamed to match a unit file's words

bullet._about: A machine gun's bullet: the wing guns, the bomber's nose gun and turrets, the heavy fighter's rear gunner, the mobile AA's quad mount and the cutter's deck guns. It draws a tracer (T5) and a hit is the hit ink, not a G3 impact (the lead's brief, gunfire-looks: 'Machine-gun bullets keep T5').
